text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS

-- The pension and health insurance authorities formed their general assemblies Monday, but both were unable to elect a president. Former Welfare Minister Pal Kovacs, supported by Mszosz, the largest union group, for the post of health insurance president, received more votes than opponent Gabor Gero, but failed to obtain the necessary two-thirds majority. The Pension Insurance Authority also failed to elect a president.

-- Top officials of the Young Democrats and the Democratic Forum met Monday to work out the technical details of a referendum aimed at preventing foreigners from obtaining cropland in Hungary. They also coordinated their opposition to a proposed government amendment to the electoral law.

-- The Finance Ministry will assign Treasury commissioners to two sections of the National Police and to eight county police stations whose debts are particularly outstanding in a bid to curb the force's indebtedness.

-- St. Stephen's Day celebrations commemorating the 11th-century King of Hungary who introduced Christianity in Hungary and founded the Hungarian state, begin this morning and continue through tomorrow night.

-- Investigators have determined that a helicopter gunship artillery shell found in a waste dump in Kaposvar belongs to the US Army. SFOR officials had denied on the weekend that the 30-mm shell could have come from them.

-- Istvan Tarlos, the mayor of Budapest's Third District, has threatened to close down the ongoing Pepsi Island music festival unless noise levels are reduced by 50 percent after midnight. Chief organiser Karoly Gerendai signed a protocol to that effect yesterday. The music festival is the largest such event in continental Europe.

-- Police have jailed the leaders of an international drug smuggling ring that brought hundreds of millions of forints worth of drugs from the Netherlands to Hungary since January of last year. Budapest police commander Attila Berta told a Monday press conference that Dutch ringleader Michael Rene and his wife are in custody, as are Hungarian Gyorgy T. and 22 accomplices.
VILLAGAZDASAG

-- More than 15,000 American SFOR soldiers will be withdrawn from Hungary and redeployed in Bosnia in two stages in the coming weeks, press officer Capt. Gregory Park, said yesterday at the Taszar air base. The first phase began late last week and lasts until August 21, involving 1,500 soldiers.
***BUSINESS***
MAGYAR NEMZET

The central budget had revenues of 1,309.9 billion forints and expenditures of 1,498.8 billion forints in the first seven months, according to Finance Ministry data reported in Magyar Nemzet. The resulting deficit of 188.9 million forints is 52.5 percent of the annual target of 359.7 million forints. The target figure excludes privatisation revenues.
ALL PAPERS

-- Retail sales ended three years of decline in June, when the total turnover was 0.9 percent higher than in the corresponding month of 1996, the Central Statistical Office reports. In the first six months, however, retail trade dropped six percent compared to the same period of last year.

-- Individual foreign currency savings increased by 8.1 billion forints in July the first increase this year, the National Bank of Hungary reported. However, the monthly 1.1 percent devaluation of the forint accounted for 5.6 billion of the total, while changes in exchange rates accounted for 1.7 billion forints.

-- The BUX Index fell 248 points yesterday, a three percent drop from the Friday's closing level of 7,799. Analysts are united in attributing the fall to the sharp decline of the Dow Jones index on Friday.
-- OTP Bank Rt. will significantly raise the registered capital of the insurance company Garancia Biztosito at its general meeting next week, Napi Gazdasag reports, citing anonymous sources.
NAPI GAZDASAG

-- The Hungarian Electricity Works (MVM Rt.) recorded a pre-tax profit of 1.2 billion forints in the first half, 500 million forints more than projected, according to preliminary calculations, economic director Dezso Csenterics told Napi Gazdasag.
